source.original_title: 06/02/2026 - Pat Klaver x Ben Byrne KFS
source.display_title: 06/02/2026 - Pat Klaver x Ben Byrne KFS — Follow Up

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: No setter is named on the call. The prospect references a prior text thread - 'So the text message string that I got, was that a viable?' - and the rep confirms it was not him: 'that was, let's see, so that wasn't for me, but I can shoot you a text.'

prospect.name: Pat Klaver
prospect.aka: Pat's iPhone - he rejoined from his phone at 00:03:26 after his laptop camera failed, and both labels are the same person
prospect.occupation: Runs an electrical department at a shipyard building ships; also owns and operates a sawmill, now at reduced hours. Works 5:30am to 2:30pm.
prospect.family_status: Divorced the previous Thursday, five days before the call. Two young children in sports - a son on a travelling baseball team, with games Monday to Thursday and weekends away. The sawmill and side work had been intended to build a family business 'for the four of us'.
prospect.training_background: Ten years military service in his twenties, ending with an injury in Iraq. Highly physically active for years through heavy manual labour at the sawmill, which he describes as roughly 90% upper body work, but has cut that back to focus on his shipyard career. Went from 240 lb to 185 lb in about seven months roughly eighteen months ago by quitting alcohol and changing his eating. Now bounces between 185 and 190. Started following Trevor about a month ago and has done a few of his free routines in the last few days, including a morning mobility routine and a physique workout that left him unable to climb stairs. Has never had a coach or trainer outside the military.
prospect.medical: Injured while serving in Iraq, which ended a ten-year military career: 'I did about 10 years until I got hurt over in Iraq, which pulled me out. So then I went through about a year and a half of rehab and back surgery and stuff like that. Got medically separated.' The nature and current status of the back surgery were never asked about. Currently reports hip and waist pain that he attributes to sitting all day: 'Pain in the hips from either sitting all day or lack of.' The pain does not appear during exercise. Previously drank heavily - describes reaching 240 lb 'due to Irish whiskey' - and has since stopped almost entirely. No current clinician involvement was mentioned and no clearance was sought.

signals: The rep named it on the call and the prospect confirmed it: 'Kind of like a rebuilding phase then.' 'Yeah. Yeah, for sure.'
Explicitly measuring himself against a former self: 'just picking up a 12-kilo kettlebell this morning, it was like, wow, this feels really heavy when it, back in my prime, it wasn't'
'my chest and shoulders used to be well more defined, broader from years ago'
Lost ground to a hard season rather than to neglect - the sawmill work that kept him in shape was scaled back, and a divorce landed five days before the call

Frames training as the thing he can still control after the family business plan collapsed: 'Well, now it's just me trying to do it all, and I'm not going to, I can't do it all. So, but getting in shape, I can do.'
Carries the regret the archetype describes, and has already proved he can execute - he lost 55 lb and quit drinking unaided eighteen months ago

goals.text: Rebuild the chest and shoulder definition he had when he was running the sawmill full time
Get his mobility and stretching back, particularly through the hips and waist
Shred fat off the midsection while staying around 185
A rhythm and a routine he can follow and adjust over time instead of guessing
Training he can take with him on weekends away at his son's baseball tournaments
Learn correct technique up front so he does not injure himself working it out by trial and error
Get his focus, energy and confidence back - 'walk taller, stand taller'
A productive outlet after the divorce rather than sitting around sulking
Just get fit and look good in a shirt, without chasing size

pains.text: Physique and mobility declining since he cut back the manual labour that had been keeping him in shape
Hip and waist pain from sitting all day at a desk
Back surgery and eighteen months of rehab following an injury in Iraq, ending his military career in a medical separation
Divorced five days before the call, not by his choice, with the settlement not yet worked out
The family business he had been building for the four of them is no longer viable on his own
No idea how to structure training or whether lifting first thing in the morning is even right for him
Building his own routine by trial and error would take him six months he does not want to spend
No time for a gym - unwilling to spend ninety minutes and compete for machines
Finances entirely unresolved pending the divorce settlement

objections.raw_quote: Okay. That I'm going to have to think of. Not that I negate that it's worth it, but with just going through the divorce, I don't have that.
objections.rep_response: Asked permission to explore it - 'if you're open to it, we can have a conversation about what maybe you could do and then see if we can come up with something' - and got a yes. Then asked what he could do and hit a genuine wall, because the prospect does not yet know his own numbers. Offered Primal University and then a 24-month financing option. Also suggested paying before the settlement so his ex-wife would not receive half of the money.

objections.raw_quote: I honestly don't know at this point. I'd have to, I'd have to go back through my finances after this all washes out to understand what it winds up being... get half of everything, my friend.
objections.rep_response: Acknowledged the impasse honestly - 'kind of hard for me to come up with a plan if you have no idea' - and pegged the follow-up to the prospect's meeting with his lawyer in the middle of the following week. Did not run any timing play against it.

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, I'd rather be able to figure out the one-on-one. That's what matters for the most part. But... Yeah. go back to that and see what I can figure out from there.
objections.rep_response: Accepted the rejection of the lower tier without argument and moved to financing options: 'there's a bunch of different options of how we can make that work for you.' The prospect rejecting the downsell in favour of the flagship is a strong buying signal that was not built on.

objections.raw_quote: no, I'd rather pay it right up front. I hate monthly things. It drives me crazy.
objections.rep_response: Accepted without exploring. This closed off the financing route the rep had just opened and confirms the blocker is purely the unknown settlement figure, not the payment structure. Proposed label: rejects_recurring_payment_structure.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Two structures were offered. A 24-month financing option against the six-month programme: 'we do have like ways where we can split up, like a financing option where you can split up to two years, which brings it down to, you know, $2.88 a month if you do the six months or a bit more if you do the year.' The figure as transcribed is $2.88 but is evidently $288 a month; at 24 months that totals $6,912 against a $6,000 cash price, and no financing cost, interest rate or total was stated. Separately a three-month tier at $4,000 was quoted, which is $1,333 a month against the six-month rate of $1,000 a month.

evidence: No decision was reached and no payment or link was exchanged - only phone numbers, with the rep texting 'Hey Pat, it's Ben from Trevor' on the call
The blocker is genuinely external and time-bound: 'gotta go talk to my lawyer to figure out what the bottom line is of after everything flushes out, what do I wind up with?'
A concrete next date exists - he has a meeting with his lawyer in the middle of the following week and expects to know by the end of it

Strong buying signals throughout: he asked 'How do we start?' unprompted, confirmed commitment without hesitation ('I'm definitely committed. There's no doubt about that'), rejected the cheaper tier in favour of the one-on-one, and said he would rather pay in full up front
He explicitly separated value from affordability: 'Not that I negate that it's worth it, but with just going through the divorce, I don't have that'
Counter-evidence: the follow-up depends entirely on the prospect texting first, and no callback was scheduled by the rep
outcome.next_step: Prospect to meet his divorce lawyer in the middle of the following week, establish what he is left with, then text Ben. No date was put in the diary by the rep and the follow-up is entirely prospect-initiated.

notable.note: Two things need escalating. First, when the prospect said he could not afford it because of the divorce, the rep suggested buying before the settlement so his ex-wife would not get half of the money: 'Well, I mean, if you pay this before, this is one last thing that she would get.' The prospect has a lawyer meeting the following week and the settlement is unresolved. Second, a three-month tier at $4,000 was quoted that does not exist in the stated offer, alongside a 24-month financing structure whose implied total exceeds the cash price with no cost disclosed. Beyond that, the rep asked a man who had told him twenty minutes earlier that he was divorced the previous Thursday whether he needed to 'talk to the wife', and never once followed up on a disclosed back surgery and medical discharge from the military before describing progressive overload training.

quality.notes: The prospect appears under two labels - 'Pat' for the first three minutes on his laptop and 'Pat's iPhone' after he rejoined from his phone at 00:03:26 - and both are the same person. Beyond that, inversion is frequent and material: at 00:11:04 the rep's question and the prospect's 'Hips and waist' answer are merged into one rep turn; at 00:10:05 'Or, like, I guess, what's the workout that's going to look like?' is labelled to the prospect but is the rep; at 00:17:47, 00:18:05, 00:34:58 and 00:38:45 question and answer cross labels, with the rep's own text message text ('Hey Pat, it's Ben from Trevor') attributed to the prospect. Role assignment was read from content throughout.
